# Stream block style

**The question:** can a stream block drop the coloured left rule (`.stream-rule-edit` amber /
`.stream-rule-append` primary) and the action pill (`长答`/`追加`) — the chrome that reads
"generated by an agent" — and still carry the block's identity, its author · time, and readable
separation? Three variants, one hash route each:

- `#a` **quiet meta line (recommended)** — no rule, no pill. One muted `admin · 17:14:55` line per
  block; the action word (`追加`/`改正文`) appears as plain muted text only when the block is not a
  plain answer. **Cost:** none — it removes chrome and keeps every signal.
- `#b` **numbered sections** — each block opens with `#3` and the action word in muted small type,
  a hairline `border-top` between blocks, closer to a printed report's sections. **Cost:** a
  separator line and a number on every block; the busiest of the three.
- `#c` **headless** — no per-block header at all; spacing is the only separation and the timeline
  is the only place author · time lives. **Cost:** the body loses per-block attribution — on a
  phone, where the timeline is a sheet, a scrolled-to block shows neither author nor time.

## Content and how it was made

The three blocks are real, consecutive blocks 1–3 of
`~/.notebook/project/gjuoun/blackboard/stream-2026-11-02-serious-round.jsonl` (the `长答` with the
layers table, then two `追加`), rendered through the app's own `lib/markdown.ts` — not hand-written
HTML. Every variant keeps each block's `id` (the timeline still jumps), the author · time line
(A/B in the body, C in the timeline), and generous spacing. One deviation from the sketch brief:
that stream contains no fenced code block anywhere, so the mock's richest real content is block
1's table plus the inline code throughout — nothing was invented to fill the gap.
